{
  "decisions": [
    {
      "item_id": "feed:26e4a943393a1b788d1e2dae",
      "version_id": "de47f3a642088f8a087f0a6f46b95b49b6830aa108fd56ccd1dec0cf490cb5f8",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "Original October 12 practitioner reporting connects an AI coding agent to debugging a small Python app. Use “by having GPT-6 Astra Extra High in Codex run it against my new web-edit app” and the passage explaining that main-thread-only profiling would miss worker-thread activity. In 01, report this concrete profiling use; in 02, identify workload-specific sampling results rather than proven optimization or productivity gains; in 03, infer a conditional check to profile all relevant threads and inspect artifacts. The author promotes his own app and supplies no controlled comparison, correction log, or total effort.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:4194b86040a10a4eac9e887c",
      "version_id": "f6fa81764f870f94f07aec62e182fa40e3fc33d09536079532a0d241369c0820",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 9 original reporting supplies a narrow student-prototyping perspective relevant to small apps. Attribute Lance's claim, “GitHub Copilot was able to not only create a frontend in 30 minutes but also connects with the actual API itself and integrates it all together.” Pair it with “Like, nothing is working,” attributed to Vaishnavi, without implying that her failure involved Copilot. Use in 02 to distinguish a reported prototype from verified delivery. GitHub sells Copilot and selects these participants; no artifacts, full effort, follow-up maintenance, or independent timing support the speed claim or the assertion that anyone can build.",
      "piece_ids": ["02"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:50257040989ddf36da8c107e",
      "version_id": "126e7b7700183bbf6dfce1990231a8f468e9de35c1f6ac20a396cd30d761b08c",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The September 23 announcement is timely, but both bots are explicitly “available today on Teams and Enterprise plans.” Rollouts requires deployment and telemetry integrations, while Security Review is presented as an organization-level PR service. No individual-plan access or concrete solo-project implementation is established. The exploitable-bug and monitoring claims are vendor promises, not validation. Do not stretch this team-focused deployment announcement into coverage for individual developers or use it merely to add Cursor as a publisher.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:5942317efb2e306a353cac42",
      "version_id": "2b8477c36458d01b02ef31fabffdfe1ae8339b51ac8a1407d7819528f05c4151",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 14 newly reports the September 28 Copilot code-review failure, rather than merely republishing old incident material. Use the incident section: “Copilot code review could not build a review, but reported that the job had completed successfully” and the advice to request affected reviews again. This directly matters to solo developers relying on review checks. In 02, distinguish job status from delivered findings; in 03, infer checking the actual review artifact and retrying affected reviews. GitHub is the responsible vendor and controls the account; this is a specific acknowledged delivery failure, not evidence of general review accuracy. Exclude infrastructure migration metrics.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:692cdddc3a75776f8e95b61e",
      "version_id": "9989d388325b9c02093c93a19ab51a65f1e4e79d67ddc0178c659f3c0e8b931d",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "The October 14 link-blog wrapper does not establish the original date of Popcar's quoted article. The supplied excerpt offers preservation and copying predictions, not a reproducible small-project implementation or verification task; its quotation also contains a malformed omission marker. Obtain the original dated article and resolve the passage before considering a narrow implementation or licensing discussion. Do not present “Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like” as a verified capability or legal conclusion.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:6ff0735dfa2a1786602e7b58",
      "version_id": "a6cb93a068bca6b88086500d4f84badfd6255baa823a198066b04d6a8e160110",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 13 original maintainer reporting establishes an integration change for developers using the LLM CLI in scripts: “I added support to llm-gemini for the new Gemini 4 Argon model”. Use in 01 as an attributed plugin update, not proof of coding quality. In 02 and 03, use “what really matters is how many tokens a model takes to achieve a goal within an agentic harness” to motivate measuring task-level cost plus testing and correction. The author maintains the plugin; SVG examples and borrowed Artificial Analysis costs do not measure verified software delivery. Treat prices as dated reported prices requiring primary-source checks, not rankings.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:7448cf38b80ee08cf4143fd4",
      "version_id": "64d8574541e189c450fc45ce2ab562095afaade75ba96e4194e6a9cc28f36e0e",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 13 original technical reporting is usable for secret checking, not its out-of-scope model-training tutorial. Use “That efficiency made it practical to extend generic secret detection to push protection” as GitHub's explanation, bounded by the companion article's preview and plan restrictions. In 02, scrutinize “Repository owner-weighted acceptance” as customer response, not independently established security or delivery success; experimental sample sizes and uncertainty are absent. In 03, infer that context-aware alerts still require confirmation and remediation. GitHub/Microsoft built and sell the system; internal offline and A/B results are source_claim, not independent corroboration.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:8188626fadfd5a946aa62314",
      "version_id": "982c692c811e5410caa2dff44e5b8389d83b867073a3b6e561758c16cf130d3a",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "The October 13 quotation wrapper does not verify the original publication date of Geoffrey Huntley's article. The pre-commit-hook passage is concretely relevant to enforcing project conventions, but freshness must be established at the original source before use. Obtain its date and surrounding implementation details; “All of a sudden it's ten out of ten” is an unsupported success assertion, not a reproducible evaluation. Do not retain the quotation with only an age caveat.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:8364c7ff1f31cec4c606c8ad",
      "version_id": "f5a017162c52e2d29ef9475c261d9091906b32635217c64e9fb03e7e10df35f5",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The October 12 original plugin update concretely adds PID display and compatibility, but supplies no AI-assistant involvement or specific AI-assisted workflow. “Knowing the PID makes it easier to attach the new Python 3.15 profiler” is ordinary debugging-tool context, already better connected to the topic by the separate web-edit profiling account. Do not count a maintainer's adjacent tool release as evidence of an AI coding capability.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:86e64baebef7f0e23a96adbb",
      "version_id": "f0b87f5852d125e85cbeb2438fe5d0ee73e1a1bface9f1ea7031804286fb5ea1",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "The October 6 original changelog establishes a concrete individual-development capability: “You can now see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app.” Use pairing steps and “Your computer needs to stay on and online” for 01 and conditional workflow guidance in 03. The default-on setting, plugged-in/open-lid requirement, and lack of a cloud-agent requirement are material constraints. Cursor sells the product; this announcement does not establish secure pairing, accessibility, reliable unattended execution, or faster verified delivery. Check account access, permissions, connectivity, and reviewability before recommending remote supervision.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:9d0ef8ba3ddce1b55a6dca3f",
      "version_id": "8575119cd60816d0cd6c477201ca1ae2245015a6a27d45f5af8b9da87e6c352c",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 7 original product reporting matters to solo developers through the announced “/security-review command for the Copilot CLI and Copilot App”, explicitly described as not requiring an organization's Secret Protection plan. In 01, distinguish that announcement from organization push protection, which is “currently in private preview” with a later rollout and AI credits. In 02, use “no statistically detectable trend regarding per-push prevalence” to limit, not settle, claims that AI causes carelessness: aggregate screened pushes do not isolate agent causation. In 03, propose checking command availability, credit attribution, and revocation procedures. This is a commercially interested product manager's account, not independent security validation.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:9e3099b85951738510dd7533",
      "version_id": "754cbbbbef0fdf63f52b8ef6428375ee7418da83b3001588ad78d50c265ee276",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 5 original reporting announces ReviewBench and supplies useful evaluation limits for developers choosing review assistance. Use “219 pull requests from 187 public open source licensed repositories spanning 19 languages” and the deliberate reduction of tiny single-file changes. In 01 report availability; in 02 contrast benchmark scope with small-project needs and note that addressed rate is judged by an LLM, not correctness; in 03 infer checking severity, false positives, missed bugs, and local tasks. GitHub/Microsoft evaluate their own product; senior-engineer auditing is internal, not an independent publisher. Relative A/B improvements lack sufficient supplied detail for endorsement as general effectiveness.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:a580349211f2b7c7e573522d",
      "version_id": "35703ce496030cdef297127607f6dc1329308a64ad44208f582ebada52d735da",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The October 6 original report concerns GitHub's distributed storage redesign for large teams and agent fleets. Its own passage identifies “an organization running thousands of agents against a single codebase” as the target. Claims of benefits to students are prospective, with no concrete individual-project capability or verified delivery implication demonstrated. Commit counts and “up to 35 times higher write throughput” are vendor infrastructure metrics, not evidence of successful AI-assisted development. Enterprise-scale architecture is outside this series.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:ab5eed4687f96de62086dece",
      "version_id": "e47a93da123115f79f33e590116df276493faddff7511ac968dd1ecb7545192b",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "The October 2 original advice has a narrow review use despite its career framing. Use “Ask a second AI model to critique the first model's work, then use your own judgment to evaluate both responses” and the hypothetical SQL duplicate-timestamp example. In 02, distinguish the hypothetical and Rubber Duck product description from evidence that independent review catches more bugs; in 03, present second-model critique as an optional check alongside executable tests and human judgment. GitHub markets Copilot, and no comparative artifacts, costs, or failure rates support its time-saving or second-perspective effectiveness assertions.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:b354478beef4b8f5c34de37f",
      "version_id": "2dd822203ebc0a1357feb6d241caaec0632a49ea38c250fabb8a5976a5932a73",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 12 original practitioner reporting describes a small Python app built with Codex for a concrete requirement: editing credentials “without round-tripping those credentials through the LLM itself.” Use the Tailscale intention and CodeMirror 6 mobile-editor choice in 01 as an attributed implementation anecdote. In 02, distinguish intended secret separation from audited confidentiality; in 03, infer checking filesystem scope, authentication, network exposure, logs, and backups before trying a similar workflow. The author promotes his own early app; no security audit, test results, or total build-and-correction effort is supplied. It is not a security endorsement.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:c15f6182059e3b795d1a52ce",
      "version_id": "c410af6157583580b670a5f6d145915c7bbb8485b3a7de9cc4d75e6fccc35893",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 8 newly published interview supplies an attributed verification practice relevant to checking security findings in small apps: “always verify what the AI gives you and never submit a finding you haven't confirmed yourself.” Use in 02 to bound the researcher's unmeasured productivity assertion and in 03 to support reproducing findings before acting. The feature-first misuse approach also informs authorization testing. GitHub selected and publishes a rewarded VIP researcher, so this is not an independent publisher or representative novice account. No disclosed AI setup, artifacts, timings, or unsuccessful findings establish general gains.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:cb7b5ad427d92eea91c444e3",
      "version_id": "475fa6853375bad114a4206b531aa56179d622a16e0be249f4d4dfb767d01e77",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The October 13 marketplace announcement lists integrations and an app-publishing process, but does not demonstrate a concrete AI-assisted requirement, implementation, testing, or debugging workflow for an individual project. The final plugin sentence promises documentation answers and port planning without an example or artifact. Cursor and listed partners have ecosystem-growth incentives; integration counts do not establish verified delivery benefits. Do not turn a general marketplace expansion into an AI-coding development merely because it is recent.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:cf03c7a3f4b088a2edc02435",
      "version_id": "ce3ba8e98287570eede60498d4cc63b57b85ff51d389037593acb2301851d5d9",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "October 14 original reporting offers concrete API design, privacy, and query-cost lessons for data-tool developers, but contains no substantive AI coding-assistant connection. AI-related titles occur only in related-post navigation. The star-history endpoint and request reductions cannot establish an assistant capability or practice, and popularity must not substitute for successful delivery. Useful general engineering content remains outside this specific series.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:dbe23f001a073722b9cecf6d",
      "version_id": "66c209040e72efd8fe6b6b823e1b16a0e93bffccf043a92d8341425e631936fe",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The October 12 original Python release discussion is useful general implementation and debugging guidance, but does not describe AI-assisted coding or verification. The LLM CLI startup example concerns plugin imports, not an assistant's performance or delivery workflow. The separate web-edit profiling item provides the actual AI-agent connection. Do not inflate the series with a language release or borrowed Fibonacci timing results that do not answer its central question.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:f4e5f15fa292a88ed95d2678",
      "version_id": "6b9d5de94367e8534f98b1b65a6d8168789a5f5f19c3fb946a1df8577b871b02",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "Accept only the identifiable new October 13 practitioner observation: “I've been trying adversarial review in my own projects recently, where you have a model try and find flaws (I often play Claude and GPT off against each other).” In 02, treat it as an attributed observation without task artifacts or measured results; in 03, frame adversarial critique as a trial requiring human triage and checks for unnecessary complexity. The author is an experienced enthusiast, not a novice sample. Defer the embedded Anthropic passages pending their original date; exclude enterprise source-control scale, merge counts, and speculative model-release causation.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:f8fa0331a2b3ce4696b878a2",
      "version_id": "a0ac872c91e89fad8413b83b3c5683bf89c547a0fcc88f0f3f56d7645592e8a3",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 12 original tutorial gives exact implementation surfaces for solo repositories: “Add a .github/copilot-instructions.md file”, the .github/skills quality-checks example, and the Playwright MCP section. Use in 03 to propose recording actual test commands, reviewing borrowed skills, limiting tool access, and checking browser-test evidence. In 02, distinguish instructions and browser interaction from enforced compliance or exhaustive verification. GitHub sells Copilot; the hypothetical workflow supplies no completed artifact or causal evaluation. This is newly published guidance, not evidence that all described features launched within the window. Accessibility-agent guidance is not an accessibility-user perspective.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:feb6c84e7898dbd8f4bb63c4",
      "version_id": "b0e717b1a48d0b74866954f18422dfa5983092b7e6d7c1ed0080d9301de41548",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "October 12 original reporting announces a model plugin update, but the supplied substance evaluates pelican drawings and repeats an external intelligence-score comparison. It provides no concrete coding, debugging, testing, or verified-delivery cost use for individual projects. “I updated my llm-meta-ai plugin for the new model” alone does not justify a general model-release listing in this evidence-led series. Do not translate SVG quality or benchmark equivalence into software-development effectiveness.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "podcast:77e8022a7eaa2d6ba037add3",
      "version_id": "67c770e529783a6ba8fa95c166241071cf1074482e8b475636d35d51f94dc801",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "The September 19 publication passes the September 15–October 14 UTC filter, but the underlying recording date is unresolved. If verified, s00206–s00228 offer a relevant attributed account of AI struggling in a debt-heavy codebase, while s00074–s00083 illustrate checking beyond a form's happy path. These do not establish that AI generally causes debt or makes maintainability unimportant; the opening Reddit quotation is not independent evidence. Obtain recording provenance and verify quotations against retained audio before assigning pieces. The hosts' agency experience is not representative of individual beginners, and sponsorship status is not established here.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "podcast:acc83661b4084b701efe6573",
      "version_id": "d30ec05b567a9c16691e94f84c0c309050357ceea62781c3afa91b62697aed23",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "September 26 publication and s00015–s00017, identifying yesterday as Tuesday, September 22nd, place recording on September 23 within the window. Use s00063–s00091 for the host's disclosed subscription, short tasks, model switching, and check-ins; use s00114–s00141 for longer orchestration exhausting usage. In 01 report an attributed workflow change; in 02 contrast usable quotas with model capability; in 03 infer budgeting complete tasks and verification. These agency practitioners offer no controlled comparison, billing logs, or artifact-based correctness evaluation. Exclude unverified price reductions, intelligence rankings, and “half” usage claims as facts. Commercial relationships are not established by the supplied segments.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "podcast:eca97e89dd5c8ca065832a7c",
      "version_id": "c478f9f69248c435b2adb8b391778d4c80f2e45462d9e2adf069e3d90dbc4b13",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "September 24 publication is in-window, but summit promotion and relative conference references do not resolve the recording date. Most content is excluded enterprise deployment. A possible narrow use is the attributed repository-review workflow in s00313–s00321, not proof of security effectiveness or a recommendation to adopt Tanzu. Verify recording provenance and any proposed exact passage first. Disclose the guest's Broadcom Tanzu marketing role, the host's Prediction Guard leadership, its operational support in s00783–s00785, and the promotional read. Do not count this recording as independent validation of vendor claims or use it to satisfy publisher quotas.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "podcast:eeed0f015cce2544ea10954e",
      "version_id": "29f402d35d089e7a41b140c97199c03e496ca1d1d6a1daa9ef90859f07ed1fc9",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "October 3 publication is recent, but the recording date remains unresolved. Potentially relevant passages are s00107–s00135 on an unfinished TCG app and learning its API, s00176–s00193 on reviewing user-data security, and s00428–s00455 on prioritizing bounded experiments. Obtain recording provenance before use. These are practitioner opinions and an uncompleted project, not proof that skilled labor or experimentation is nearly free. The hosts run an agency and promote their own media; no full cost accounting or verified delivery artifact supports the headline. Preserve the tension between rapid prototyping and understanding integrations rather than endorsing either extreme.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "podcast:ff459ee5091a52baed0781c2",
      "version_id": "f13d1e52e611d96240a2a68bbeed894f342bf62304250e51c2f40046b743d8c7",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "October 13 upload does not resolve recording freshness: s00058 says “So we're in September of 2026.” That month straddles the September 15 cutoff; relative model-release references do not independently establish a date. Seek original recording provenance before using s00798–s00838 on small tasks and manual verification or s00850–s00887 on agent-run tests followed by human checks. Disclose Scrimba promotion and patron support if later used. Unsupported developer-percentile and 10x claims, trust-based reductions in review, and unfinished production-loop ambitions require scrutiny, not endorsement. The useful workflow passages do not override the unresolved date.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "youtube:I_KVMFrUtPk",
      "version_id": "32127ba326b69f66e546248ae61d0c9ae872aafa14680d9a34af8cd4d398d84b",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "The recording explicitly identifies September 30th, 2026 in s00042–s00044. Use s00113–s00135 as an attributed demonstration of a private-file session blocking a public GitHub issue pending approval, relevant to protecting small-project code. In 01 report the demonstrated tool boundary; in 02 retain preview, task-completion, and token-cost qualifications in s00138–s00148 as unverified source claims; in 03 propose checking classifications, tool coverage, bypasses, and approval behavior on harmless fixtures. Open Appa sponsors the video, disclosed in s00034–s00035. Product names vary in transcription: preserve supplied wording and verify against audio before quoting. Exclude the unsourced government incident and universal protection claims.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "youtube:J37YeB63LVI",
      "version_id": "5e553751c72b186f48fe15f7cca08e99ca4a7ec7c6436cbf307ff9cc94866405",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "The October 14 upload supplies substantial relevant demonstration material, but no resolved original recording date. Verify provenance before using s00237–s00267 for a failed commit followed by automatic formatting, s00393–s00429 for a deliberately failing test, and s00797–s00847 for unresolved migration/plugin errors. These could support concrete setup, limitations, and conditional next checks across the series, not the headline's universal replacement claim or guaranteed type safety. Transcript command and tool names also need audio/screen verification before executable guidance. The creator promotes related tutorials; sponsorship is not established in the supplied transcript. Do not discard the demonstrations merely for lacking causal productivity proof.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "youtube:No-JPdFvYWU",
      "version_id": "524cd74d3c1a5bc817fa547d0b641eb66a9d6b91b078accbcf33eea079718ac4",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "s00023–s00024 explicitly date this original report October 1st, 2026. Use s00047–s00061 as secondary, attributed reporting of a vendor API-removal demo involving dependency tracing, tests, PRs, and a live-demo difficulty; use s00152–s00157 as a sponsored, attributed OpenCode routing-integration example. In 01 describe those reported workflows, in 02 distinguish demonstration from verified delivery, and in 03 propose checking routing errors, test artifacts, correction effort, and total cost. Fastly Labs sponsors the video, disclosed in s00139–s00141. Exclude training instructions, earnings promises, speed/cost rankings, and unverified pricing as facts; verify primary announcements before definitive availability guidance.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "youtube:QZVzuq28eFw",
      "version_id": "de7c531c5808c2edf9e55a4227bb0fb839e17d68858e02763b16dc52110dce32",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "s00022–s00024 explicitly date the recording October 14th, 2026. Accept only s00134–s00144: the sponsored Codesmith launch description and attributed example of adding a provider, opening PRs across two repositories, and responding to failed tests or review comments. This is relevant to small-app implementation and debugging. In 01 report the sponsored capability description; in 02 disclose absent diffs, test logs, costs, and independent validation; in 03 propose checking permissions, secret handling, both PRs, and rerun results. Blacksmith sponsorship is explicit in s00128–s00130. Omit runner-performance claims and the unrelated criminal allegations entirely.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "youtube:_5p1_TNSWqQ",
      "version_id": "c08316a058448ab9bab809a168b6e00bd41bf8718a9dc4efc3901524534035f9",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "s00025–s00027 explicitly date the recording October 5th, 2026. Exclude its model-training main story. Narrowly use s00151–s00154 on inspecting a live CI runner and providing build data to an agent, plus s00160–s00168 describing an agent VM with code, tests, databases, and network controls. These are sponsored workflow descriptions relevant to reproducing small-project failures, not independently tested capabilities. In 02 disclose Namespace sponsorship from s00145–s00148 and absent artifacts; in 03 infer checking environment parity, access controls, retained logs, and cost before use. No newly launched feature is established, so do not assign 01. Omit benchmark ranking, fastest-runner, and safety guarantees.",

    {

      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "s00039–s00040 explicitly date the recording October 12th, 2026. Use s00059–s00082 for the creator's attempted FilmCraft editing task, reported lag, and transition comparison: a concrete failure case contrasting interface resemblance with usable delivery. In 02 this challenges clone-completion rhetoric without proving AI caused the defects; in 03 infer testing representative end-to-end behavior before declaring a project finished. Exclude universal decompilation/open-source claims, licensing conclusions, and the explicitly invented benchmark. Across the accepted set, independent controlled research and first-time, unsuccessful-project, budget-constrained, and accessibility-user coverage remain insufficient; these selections do not establish completed pieces or student review, policy revision, rerun comparison, and final approval.",
